summary: Pulled Eurostat Comext DS-045409 monthly (freq M, DE, EXT_EU27_2020) for CN 72, 7208 and 7204, imports and exports, value and mass, 2025-01 to 2026-08. The latest month is August 2026 and the dataset stamp is 2026-10-16. The like-for-like comparison (Jan-Aug 2026 vs Jan-Aug 2025) for Chapter 72 is: imports +7.7% in tonnes (1,108 vs 1,028 kt), -0.7% in value (EUR 1,119 m vs 1,127 m), unit value -7.9% (EUR 1,010/t vs 1,096/t). Exports are -16.3% in tonnes (2,822 vs 3,372 kt), -18.4% in value and -2.5% in unit value. Extra-EU net X-M falls from 2,343 to 1,714 kt (-26.9%). The 2026 data are provisional; Eurostat's next update is 13 Nov 2026, before the 16-18 Nov presentations. The 2025 annual and monthly data match the workbook exactly, and only the 2023 annual import value was revised, by a negligible amount. Separately labelled, WV Stahl crude steel is 23,902 kt for Jan-Aug 2026 (+6.3%), and the 2025 total was revised from 34.1 to 34.3 Mt. Nothing was estimated; all folder outputs are under data/trade_2026 and no git was run.

key_facts.label: Eurostat revision / provisional policy for Comext detailed data
key_facts.value: Previously published data are revised whenever revised national data arrive. Routine and unscheduled revisions come mainly from late declarations (chiefly intra-EU), errors and omissions, and can also affect extra-EU data. Monthly data are generally considered final in October of the following reference year. The 16 Oct 2026 news release states its figures are provisional. The API gives no per-observation flags.

caveats: 2026 monthly values are provisional. Eurostat says routine and unscheduled revisions occur and that monthly data are generally final in October of the following year. The API carries no per-observation status flags, so 2025 should be called 'at or close to final', not 'final'. The 13 Nov 2026 update will restate Jan-Aug and add September.

The 13 Nov 2026 next-release date comes from the Eurostat euro-indicator page. That the Comext detailed dataset updates the same day is inferred from the metadata (detailed data published on the news-release date) and from the 16 Oct stamp matching the 16 Oct release.

Scope: direct extra-EU27 (fixed 2020 composition) trade of Germany in Chapter 72, including scrap and excluding Chapter 73 and ore. It is not the CBAM base, not national-accounts NX, and not the same universe as the all-partner 'steel mill products' of Dataset B. Unit values are product-mix indicators. Data are nominal and not seasonally or calendar adjusted.

The tiny CN 7208 base makes percentage changes meaningless (+488% in tonnes); quote kilotonnes. Single-month YoY swings are large (-44% to +49% for imports). The Jan-Jun vs Jul-Aug split is descriptive only, and the 1 July 2026 start of the new EU steel trade-defence instrument comes from WV Stahl press releases (an industry association), not from a Council or Commission text I opened.

The eight-month comparison mixes the definitive CBAM period (from 1 Jan 2026), the new quota (from 1 Jul 2026), weak domestic demand and energy or macro effects. It does not support any causal statement about ETS or CBAM.

WV Stahl is an industry association, and its monthly figures are preliminary; the 2025 total was just revised (34.1 to 34.3 Mt). Press releases before 10 Aug 2026 appear to use the unrevised 2025 base (for H1: +8.9% published vs +8.2% against the revised months). The September 2026 figure was not yet published at retrieval. Crude steel is a production measure and must not be combined with the Comext trade flows.

The Eurostat metadata page was last updated 6 Oct 2025, so the revision-policy text is the latest statement found but is a year old. Destatis was checked only for context (press release 356 of 8 Oct 2026 has no iron and steel line) and is not used.

Two WV Stahl press-page items were seen only as headlines and not read in full: 13 Oct 2026 (worldsteel outlook, German demand lagging) and 16 Oct 2026 (automotive-package steel credit versus the German-French super-credit proposal). The latter may matter for S13's demand-side suggestions.
This task did not cover the 1999-2025 extra-EU export series or the other open items; only data/trade_2026 was written, and no git was run.
